subject: Pre-sales traffic census + token/profile questions — OrbitFoundry pilot
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@orbitfoundry.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Pre-sales traffic census + token/profile questions — OrbitFoundry pilot

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the meeting earlier — excited about the pilot scope (search + summarization endpoints). To make sure we size Dedicated appropriately, can you share a short traffic census and a few sample metrics so we can map to GPU occupancy and burst pools? Specifically: 

- Typical QPS during peak 10-minute windows (and ideal business hours).
- Expected concurrent sessions for the interactive search flow (and session timeout).
- Prompt length distribution (percentiles for prompts and expected response lengths).
- Percent of requests that are embeddings / reranking / generation.
- Any synchronous latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) you need for production.

If you have a small telemetry export, CSV or JSON is perfect — even a few days of representative logs helps. I attached a one-page intake form below to make it quick.

Next steps: once we have those numbers, Marissa (solutions) and I will run a quick sizing sketch and share a recommended reserved GPU mix and burst plan.

Thanks —
Dylan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pre-sales-intake-form.pdf (stub)]

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@orbitfoundry.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-sales traffic census + token/profile questions — OrbitFoundry pilot

Dylan —

Appreciate the concise checklist. I exported a small sample and included a quick summary below; full CSV attached. High level: search is our main path (~78% of calls), summarization is spiky (campaign-driven).

Summary (last 7 days sample):
- Peak 10-min QPS: 420 requests
- Typical sustained QPS (day): 120–180 requests
- Concurrent interactive sessions (peak): ~85 (session = user open + active queries within 30s)
- Prompt lengths (tokens): median 32, 90th 180, max 1,100 (long tail from doc-summaries)
- Response lengths (tokens): median 24, 90th 210, max 2,400
- Traffic split: generation 15%, embeddings 5%, reranking 2%, search/generation combined ~78%
- Target latency SLOs: p95 < 800ms for search queries; p99 < 2s for high-priority flows

Notes:
- We use session affinity in our app for a subset of users — about 12% of traffic sticks to the same session id.
- We do occasional batch jobs (daily indexing) that will push long responses off-hours.

Attachment: orbitfoundry-telemetry-sample.csv (columns: ts, path, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_id, latency_ms, user_tier)

Happy to hop on a short call if you want me to walk through the CSV.

—Elena
Director of Platform, OrbitFoundry

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@orbitfoundry.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-sales traffic census + token/profile questions — OrbitFoundry pilot

Elena — thanks, this is great and the CSV is exactly what we need. A couple of quick clarifying questions before Marissa and I run the sizing sketch: 

1) For the peak 10-minQPS = 420, is that dominated by short-search queries (~<64 tokens), or does it include many of the long-tail doc summarization requests? If possible, could you split the peak window by endpoint/path in the CSV?

2) You mentioned session affinity for 12% of traffic — do those sessions tend to re-use KV cache across calls (i.e., repeated context), or are they independent requests?

3) For the daily batch indexing that produces long responses, do you expect that to be parallel across many workers (fan-out) or sequential? We want to know whether burst capacity should consider concurrent long-response workers.

If you prefer, Marissa and I can sketch two sizing options: (A) conservative (reserve for peak sustained + 20% buffer) vs (B) optimized (reserve for sustained and rely on burst capacity and preemptible pools for the long-tail). Either way, we'll include suggested GPU SKUs and expected p95 token latency estimates.

Would be helpful if you can mark the CSV rows with path=/search vs /summarize where possible — otherwise we'll infer.

Thanks —
Dylan

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: OrbitFoundry sizing intake — quick summary and ask

Marissa — forwarding OrbitFoundry's telemetry sample (attached) and Elena's summary above. Quick read + asks for the sizing sketch: 

Key signals
- Peak 10-min QPS: 420 (likely mixed short search + some long summaries)
- Sustained day QPS: 120–180
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~85 (12% session affinity)
- Prompt tokens median 32 / 90th 180 / max 1,100
- Response tokens median 24 / 90th 210 / max 2,400
- Traffic mix heavy on search/generation 
- p95 SLO target: 800ms (search) / p99 2s

Sizing asks
- Can you run a quick sketch for both Conservative and Optimized paths outlined below? Include: GPU SKU mix, baseline reserved fleet (nodes + expected occupancy), burst pool strategy (size + fallback to hosted), and KV cache sizing assumptions. Please assume US region (GCP us-west2) and no special compliance constraints.

Conservative: reserve for peak 10-min QPS + 20% buffer, aim p95 headroom 1.2x
Optimized: reserve for sustained QPS, rely on burst for 10-min peaks, add quantization on summarization model to reduce token cost

Also: flag anything that would push us to propose Dedicated+Private (e.g., >2x long-response concurrency or heavy session stickiness requiring tenant isolation).

If you can get this back by EOD tomorrow I'll turn it into a proposal for Elena — low-risk ask but they care about tight p95.

Thanks —
Dylan
